info.p: We count. Will you count with us?

Since 2025, we have come together in our millions to demand Trump leave the White House before the end of his second term. But too many of our actions go uncounted, undocumented, or misrepresented. If a protest isn’t counted, did it really happen? We believe every protest, and every one of us protesters, counts.

We use real numbers to tell our movement’s story. Our dashboard visualizes over 11,300 anti-Trump protests, showing the true scope and power behind us. Imagine seeing our largest number of participants in a single day of protest (over 3 million), our percentage of participation compared to the 3.5% Rule (1.67%), or the overwhelming percentage of protests with no injuries (99.8%), arrests (99.4%), or property damage (99.7%). Our numbers show the scale, the solidarity, and the nonviolent nature of our movement.

When we count by designating counters, getting accurate crowd counts, and creating public sources, our actions shape the record, inform the media, and build momentum of dissent. The Crowd Counting Consortium (CCC), an independent public project out of Harvard University in conjunction with the University of Connecticut, collects data on protests that meet qualifying criteria. By making sure our protests are counted, we measure not just size (mass) but also the velocity of our movement. Mass multiplied by frequency (velocity) equals our momentum of dissent, and it’s what builds the power to force an "irregular leader exit" (Trump's resignation).

We empower organizers: before any of our protests, we plan how we will count the crowds. During our protests, we tally the crowds and save the details. Afterward, we create public sources and, if possible, submit to CCC so our movement is truly seen. It's also important that we follow up and make corrections as needed with the CCC.

Coalitions and organizations can use our materials to share these best practices and our dashboard to inspire action. The media can report the real numbers, not the lore [myths?]. Every participant can be counted, no registration required.
We count our protests. We count each protester. We count because we believe our movement matters and together, we can make history with our counts. Protests count. And so do we!
